reprokit: reproduce and check results when raw data cannot be shared

Source: R/reprokit-package.R
reprokit-package.Rd

Sharing raw data remains the standard. When sharing is genuinely impossible, reprokit says what the minimum is that authors owe their readers, and what those readers lose. It also lets readers check whether the numbers a paper reports are consistent with each other.

Details

Two directions use the same statistics.

Share (you cannot share the raw data):

  • sufficient_stats() says whether summary statistics suffice and what to publish, and stores them. It never errors on the verdict, and its print narrates the verdict, what to publish and what readers lose. It takes a fitted model or result, a formula, or, for a mediation, two lm fits.

  • appendix() writes the appendix for the paper from the same input. reprokit states what readers lose, from the test; you do not fill that in. A sharing_reason, in your own words, is optional: without one appendix() gives a warning and the appendix says that no reason was stated.

Check (you are reading a paper):

  • check_reported() tests whether reported numbers are consistent with each other, allowing for rounding, for the test you name.

An inconsistency means the numbers cannot all be correct as reported. It does not say which number is wrong or why.

Reference: coverage_table() lists which tests are covered and what each needs, and conventions() the effect-size conventions and sums-of-squares types you can declare. See also handlers(), quantity_names() and verdicts().
